operations.name: Tom Melville

expected.charges: Federal destruction of government property — May 17, 1968 Catonsville draft-board raid
expected.sentence:
3 years federal prison

Verdict as recorded: Yes — federal jury verdict, U.S. District Court for the District of Maryland, October 10, 1968

Baltimore Magazine’s 2018 retrospective, based on interviews with surviving participants, reports 18 months actually served for the Catonsville case. This reported case-level duration replaces the incomplete seven-day counter; the initial May 17-24, 1968 pretrial dates remain in the record. The seven pretrial days are not added again to the reported total. Exact later prison release dates remain unresolved; no calendar endpoint is calculated from the reported months.

operations.source: Digital Maryland Catonsville Nine documentary exhibit, individual sentencing: https://c9.digitalmaryland.org/page.php?ID=25 . Corroborated by Shawn Francis Peters, The Catonsville Nine, chapter 18, https://academic.oup.com/book/6063/chapter-abstract/149515034 . Original 1968 case only; no later admission/release day inferred.

operations.name: Benjamin Weiss

expected.charges: Conspiracy to advocate overthrow of the government (Smith Act)
expected.sentence:
One of the Philadelphia Smith Act defendants. Arrested and indicted in 1953, convicted at trial in 1954. On appeal the Third Circuit found the evidence insufficient as to Weiss and directed that a judgment of acquittal be entered rather than ordering a retrial.

Verdict as recorded: Convicted at trial in 1954; Third Circuit directed a judgment of acquittal on appeal (1957)

updates.prosecutor: W. Wilson White; Marvin B. Segal; Lawrence P. McGauley; Carl G. Coben; William F. Tompkins; Harold K. Wood; Philip R. Monahan; Doris H. Spangenburg; Anthony A. Ambrosio (counsel for the United States on appeal)

operations.source: Primary United States v. Kuzma et al., 249 F.2d 619: https://law.resource.org/pub/us/case/reporter/F2/249/249.F2d.619.11655-11663_1.html . Benjamin Weiss named appellant; counsel role qualified. Appellate acquittal not assumed physical release.

operations.name: Eve Tetaz

expected.charges: Disruption of Congress / disorderly conduct — May 21, 2009 Senate hearing protest
expected.sentence: Convicted with Barfield and Perry in October 2009. On January 25, 2010 Judge Lynn Liebovitz imposed 25 days in D.C. Jail beginning that day, another 50 days suspended, and one year of probation with a Capitol Hill stay-away order. The contemporary Baltimore Nonviolence Center report confirms actual commencement, not merely an advance schedule. The individual release day is not established. Source: https://baltimorenonviolencecenter.blogspot.com/2010/01/eve-tetaz-is-in-dc-jail.html

operations.source: Contemporary support report of actual January 25, 2010 sentencing: https://baltimorenonviolencecenter.blogspot.com/2010/01/eve-tetaz-is-in-dc-jail.html . Individually names judge. Only 2009 Senate hearing protest case; existing admission preserved and release remains unresolved.
